# DumpCat API reference

DumpCat 1.9.0 at https://backup.example.com backs up MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL and SQL Server databases on schedules, archives their logs for point-in-time recovery, restores them and tests backups with restore drills. This reference is written by the server itself and lists every route it serves: `GET https://backup.example.com/api/docs.md`.

## Authentication

- Create an API token in the web UI: **API & MCP → New token** (or `POST /api/me/tokens`). Send it with every request:
  `Authorization: Bearer mv_…`. A token acts as the account that created it.
- **Read-only** tokens (the default) can call every `GET` route except downloads and OAuth, plus `POST /api/cron/preview` and `POST /api/pitr/plan`: they look and change nothing. **Full-access** tokens can do everything the account's role can. **Manage** tokens are full-access tokens that MCP also lets set up and change jobs, drills, servers and storages; over the REST API they are the same as full access.
- Roles, from least to most: viewer (looks), operator (runs backups, restores, manages servers, storages, jobs and drills), admin (users, settings, notifications, agents, WireGuard, updates). Each route below names the lowest role it needs.
- Requests with a token need no CSRF header (the web UI's session sends `X-CSRF-Token` on changes).

## Conventions

- JSON in and out. A request with a body must send `Content-Type: application/json`.
- Errors answer an HTTP status and `{"error": "message"}`: 400 invalid input, 401 no or invalid token, 403 role too low or read-only token, 404 not found, 409 conflict (e.g. the job is already running), 415 not JSON, 429 too many attempts, 503 while DumpCat updates itself.
- Ids are numbers. Times are RFC 3339 (`2026-10-20T14:37:11+07:00`).
- Paged lists answer `{"items": [...], "total": n}` and take `limit` and `offset`.
- Logs answer `{"data": "…", "next": n}`; pass `next` back as `offset` to follow a running task, or `tail=1` to start at the end.
- Secrets (database passwords, passphrases, storage keys, webhook addresses, tokens) are never returned.
- Long tasks (backups, verifications, restores, drills) start in the background: the answer is the new object; poll it until `status` is no longer `queued` or `running`.
- Every change is written to the audit log with the account's name.

## Examples

```bash
TOKEN=mv_xxxxxxxx
# what needs attention
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://backup.example.com/api/dashboard
# the failed backups of job 1
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://backup.example.com/api/runs?job_id=1&status=failed"
# why backup 42 failed: its error, then the end of its log
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://backup.example.com/api/runs/42
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://backup.example.com/api/runs/42/log?tail=1"
# run job 1 now (full-access token)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"full"}' https://backup.example.com/api/jobs/1/run
```

## AI assistants (MCP)

DumpCat is an MCP server: `https://backup.example.com/api/mcp` (streamable HTTP, header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`). For clients that start a local command, `dumpcat mcp` forwards stdio to it (settings `DUMPCAT_MCP_URL`, `DUMPCAT_MCP_TOKEN`). Each tool call runs the REST request named below with the token: the same role check, read-only rule and audit log. A full-access token starts backups, verifications, drills and storage tests; the tools that set up and change jobs, drills, servers and storages need a token with Manage access. Restores, deletions and settings are not available over MCP, and no tool takes or returns a secret (password, key, passphrase): a tool that leaves one unset answers `finish_url`, the web UI page where the user enters it.

| Tool | What it does | Role | Token | REST request |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `get_overview` | Start here | viewer | read-only or full | `GET /api/dashboard` |
| `get_monitoring` | Monitoring status and alerts: for every job, whether its newest successful backup is fresh or overdue (stale, due_at: the same rule as DumpCat's freshness alerts and /metrics); the state of continuous log archiving (MySQL binlogs, PostgreSQL WAL, SQL Server log backups): streaming or failing, files waiting for upload, archive lag; and the active warnings | viewer | read-only or full | `GET /api/dashboard` |
| `list_servers` | The database servers DumpCat backs up or restores to: engine (mysql = MySQL, MariaDB, Percona; postgres = PostgreSQL; mssql = SQL Server), address, user, TLS mode, detected version, and how DumpCat reaches them (directly, or through an agent or WireGuard peer by id) | viewer | read-only or full | `GET /api/servers` |
| `get_server` | One database server | viewer | read-only or full | `GET /api/servers/{id}` |
| `list_jobs` | The backup jobs: server, method, databases, schedules (cron), compression, encryption, storage targets, retention, options (verification, log archiving, max age), enabled or running, the last run, the next run and the last restore drill | viewer | read-only or full | `GET /api/jobs` |
| `get_job` | One backup job with its configuration, whether it is running, its last run, next run and last restore drill | viewer | read-only or full | `GET /api/jobs/{id}` |
| `list_backups` | Backups (each run of a job), newest first, with total for paging | viewer | read-only or full | `GET /api/runs` |
| `get_backup` | One backup in detail: status, error, timings, sizes, its databases and files, where it is stored and the state of each copy, its verification and restore drill results, its incremental chain, and live progress while it runs | viewer | read-only or full | `GET /api/runs/{id}` |
| `get_log` | The last lines of a task's log, to see why something failed or how far it got | viewer | read-only or full | `GET /api/runs/{id}/log` |
| `list_restores` | Restores that were run from the web UI or API, newest first: backup, target server, status and error | viewer | read-only or full | `GET /api/restores` |
| `get_restore` | One restore: backup, target server, options, status, error, and live progress while it runs | viewer | read-only or full | `GET /api/restores/{id}` |
| `list_drills` | Restore drills: tests that restore a job's backup into a sandbox server under temporary names and check it (tables, row counts, SQL assertions, time to restore) | viewer | read-only or full | `GET /api/drills` |
| `list_drill_runs` | Results of restore drills, newest first: passed, failed or partial (temporary databases left behind), with summary and error | viewer | read-only or full | `GET /api/drill-runs` |
| `get_drill_run` | One restore drill run: every check with its result, restore and check durations, the databases, temporary databases left behind, the error, and live progress while it runs | viewer | read-only or full | `GET /api/drill-runs/{id}` |
| `plan_pitr` | Preview a point-in-time recovery; nothing is changed or restored | operator | read-only or full | `POST /api/pitr/plan` |
| `run_backup` | Start a backup of a job now, like Run now in the web UI, and return the new backup (its id is for get_backup and get_log; it runs in the background) | operator | full access | `POST /api/jobs/{id}/run` |
| `verify_backup` | Check a stored backup: read every copy (or one location) back from storage and compare each file's checksum | operator | full access | `POST /api/runs/{id}/verify` |
| `start_drill` | Run a restore drill now: restore a backup (the newest usable one, or backup_id) into the drill's sandbox server under temporary names, run its checks, then drop the temporary databases | operator | full access | `POST /api/drills/{id}/run` |
| `list_storages` | Where backups are stored: local folders, S3, Google Drive, OneDrive, SFTP and the others, with the result of their last test and the jobs that use them | viewer | read-only or full | `GET /api/storages` |
| `get_storage` | One storage with its settings (secrets never: secrets_set and secrets_not_set name them) and the result of its last test | viewer | read-only or full | `GET /api/storages/{id}` |
| `list_storage_types` | The kinds of storage DumpCat writes to and the settings of each (for create_storage): key, label, whether required, default, choices, and show_if (the setting applies only when another has one of these values) | viewer | read-only or full | `GET /api/storage-types` |
| `preview_schedule` | Check a cron expression for a job or drill schedule and show its next five times in DumpCat's time zone; changes nothing | viewer | read-only or full | `POST /api/cron/preview` |
| `test_storage` | Check a storage's settings and credentials now: write, read back and delete a small test file | operator | full access | `POST /api/storages/{id}/test` |
| `create_server` | Add a database server to back up (or to restore drills into) | operator | Manage access | `POST /api/servers` |
| `update_server` | Change a database server's settings; only the ones given change | operator | Manage access | `PUT /api/servers/{id}` |
| `create_storage` | Add a storage that backups are written to, with its settings from list_storage_types | operator | Manage access | `POST /api/storages` |
| `update_storage` | Rename a storage or change its settings; only the ones given change and saved secrets stay | operator | Manage access | `PUT /api/storages/{id}` |
| `create_job` | Create a backup job: which server, method, databases, when (cron), where to (storages) and how many to keep | operator | Manage access | `POST /api/jobs` |
| `update_job` | Change a backup job; only the settings given change (options and retention key by key; targets is the whole list) | operator | Manage access | `PUT /api/jobs/{id}` |
| `create_drill` | Create a restore drill: on a schedule, restore a job's newest backup into a sandbox server under temporary names, check tables, row counts and SQL assertions, then drop the copies | operator | Manage access | `POST /api/drills` |
| `update_drill` | Change a restore drill; only the settings given change (options key by key; assertions is the whole list) | operator | Manage access | `PUT /api/drills/{id}` |

## Routes

Paths are relative to https://backup.example.com. `{id}` is a number.

### Overview and monitoring

Start here to answer "is everything backed up?".

#### `GET /api/dashboard`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

Counts of servers, jobs and backups; every job's last result, last successful backup, freshness (`stale`, `due_at`) and next run; the tasks running now; the 12 newest backups; and the current `warnings` (failed jobs, overdue backups, log archiving problems, failed restore drills).

#### `GET /api/activity`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

The tasks running now (backups, verifications, copies, restores, drills) with their progress.

### Backup jobs

A job is what to back up (a server and its databases), how, where to and when. Create and update take a job object as `GET /api/jobs/{id}` returns it.

#### `GET /api/jobs`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

List the jobs with their schedule, storages, retention, last result and next run.

#### `POST /api/jobs`

operator · full-access token

Create a job. Answers the job with its `id`.

#### `GET /api/jobs/{id}`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

One job. The encryption passphrase is never returned.

#### `PUT /api/jobs/{id}`

operator · full-access token

Update a job (send the whole object).

#### `DELETE /api/jobs/{id}`

operator · full-access token

Delete a job. `?delete_backups=1` also deletes its backups from every storage; without it they stay listed under Backups.

#### `POST /api/jobs/{id}/run`

operator · full-access token

Start a backup now. Body (optional): `{"type": "full"}` or `{"type": "incremental"}` (physical backups). Answers the new backup; follow it with `GET /api/runs/{id}`. 409 while the job is already running.

#### `POST /api/jobs/{id}/toggle`

operator · full-access token

Turn the job's schedule on or off.

#### `POST /api/cron/preview`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

Check a cron expression and list its next run times. Body: `{"expr": "0 2 * * *"}`. Changes nothing.

### Backups

A backup (a *run*) is one execution of a job: its files with SHA-256, its copies on each storage, its verification and drills.

#### `GET /api/runs`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

List backups, newest first. Query: `job_id`, `status` (queued, running, success, partial, failed, canceled, deleted), `method`, `q` (search), `live=1` (running only), `limit` (default 50), `offset`. Answers `{"items": [...], "total": n}`.

#### `GET /api/runs/{id}`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

One backup: status, error, files with checksums, copies per storage, binlog / WAL position, verification, drills and progress.

#### `GET /api/runs/{id}/log`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

The backup's log. Query: `offset` (bytes) or `tail=1` (the last 200 KB). Answers `{"data": "…", "next": n}`: pass `next` as `offset` to follow a running backup.

#### `POST /api/runs/{id}/cancel`

operator · full-access token

Cancel a queued or running backup.

#### `POST /api/runs/{id}/verify`

operator · full-access token

Read the copies back and compare every checksum. Body (optional): `{"location_id": n}` for one copy only. Runs in the background: the result appears on the backup.

#### `POST /api/runs/{id}/delete`

operator · full-access token

Delete a backup. Body (optional): `{"location_id": n}` deletes one copy only; `{"cascade": true}` also deletes the incremental backups based on it.

#### `POST /api/runs/{id}/restore`

operator · full-access token

Start a restore. Body: `target_server_id`, `location_id` (optional), `databases` (a subset), `rename` (`{"old": "new"}`), `drop_existing` (needs `"confirm": "RESTORE"`), `restore_users`, `threads`, portability options (`strip_definer`, `convert_collations`, `skip_gtid_purged`, `no_owner`, `no_privileges`) and `pitr` (a point-in-time target, see `POST /api/pitr/plan`). Physical backups: `target_dir` (admin), `apply` (replace the datadir: admin, needs `"confirm": "RESTORE"`). Answers the restore; follow it with `GET /api/restores/{id}`.

#### `POST /api/runs/{id}/restore-check`

operator · full-access token

Compare a backup with the server it would be restored to (version, flavor, databases already there) and suggest options. Body: `{"target_server_id": n}`. Changes nothing.

#### `POST /api/runs/{id}/copy`

operator · full-access token

Copy the backup to another storage. Body: `{"storage_id": n}`.

#### `GET /api/runs/{id}/download`

operator · full-access token

Download one file of the backup. Query: `file` (a name from the backup's files), `location_id` (optional), `decode=1` (decrypt and decompress on the way).

### Restores

#### `GET /api/restores`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

List the restores that were run, with status and error.

#### `GET /api/restores/{id}`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

One restore: source backup, target, options, progress, result.

#### `GET /api/restores/{id}/log`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

The restore's log (`offset`, `tail=1`, as for backups).

#### `POST /api/restores/{id}/cancel`

operator · full-access token

Cancel a running restore.

### Log archiving and point-in-time recovery

Jobs can archive the database's log continuously (MySQL / MariaDB binlogs, PostgreSQL WAL, SQL Server log backups) to restore to any moment after a backup.

#### `GET /api/binlog`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

Every job that archives its log: streaming or failing, files waiting for upload, archive lag.

#### `GET /api/jobs/{id}/binlogs`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

The archived log files of a job (`offset` for paging).

#### `GET /api/jobs/{id}/binlog/log`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

The log of the job's archiver (`offset`, `tail=1`).

#### `POST /api/jobs/{id}/binlog/rotate`

operator · full-access token

Close the current log file now, so that everything up to now is uploaded.

#### `POST /api/jobs/{id}/binlog/restart`

operator · full-access token

Restart the job's archiver.

#### `POST /api/pitr/plan`

operator · read-only or full-access token

Preview a point-in-time recovery: the base backup it would start from and whether the archived log reaches the target. Body: `{"job_id": n, "run_id": n (optional), "target": {"type": "time", "time": "2026-10-20T14:37:11+07:00"}}`. Target types: `latest`, `time`; MySQL `position` (`file`, `pos`) and `gtid`; PostgreSQL `lsn` and `name` (a restore point); SQL Server `lsn` and `mark` (`name`: a marked transaction). Changes nothing.

### Restore drills

A drill restores a backup into a sandbox and runs checks on it, on a schedule or on demand.

#### `GET /api/drills`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

List the drills (`job_id` to filter) with their last result.

#### `POST /api/drills`

operator · full-access token

Create a drill.

#### `GET /api/drills/{id}`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

One drill.

#### `PUT /api/drills/{id}`

operator · full-access token

Update a drill.

#### `DELETE /api/drills/{id}`

operator · full-access token

Delete a drill.

#### `POST /api/drills/{id}/run`

operator · full-access token

Run the drill now. Body (optional): `{"run_id": n}` to test one backup (default: the newest). Answers the drill run.

#### `GET /api/drill-runs`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

List drill runs. Query: `drill_id`, `job_id`, `run_id`, `limit`, `offset`.

#### `GET /api/drill-runs/{id}`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

One drill run: every check with its result, the restore time (RTO).

#### `GET /api/drill-runs/{id}/log`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

The drill run's log (`offset`, `tail=1`).

#### `POST /api/drill-runs/{id}/cancel`

operator · full-access token

Cancel a running drill.

### Database servers

Passwords are never returned; on update, an empty password keeps the stored one.

#### `GET /api/servers`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

List the database servers.

#### `POST /api/servers`

operator · full-access token

Add a server (name, engine, host, port, username, password, connection mode, …).

#### `POST /api/servers/test`

operator · full-access token

Test the connection of unsaved settings (same body as creating): version, missing privileges, usable backup methods.

#### `GET /api/servers/{id}`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

One server.

#### `PUT /api/servers/{id}`

operator · full-access token

Update a server.

#### `DELETE /api/servers/{id}`

operator · full-access token

Delete a server.

#### `GET /api/servers/{id}/info`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

Connect now and inspect: version, datadir, databases and their sizes (`sizes=0` skips the sizes), usable methods.

#### `GET /api/engines`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

The supported database engines with their backup methods, restore options and log archiving.

### Agents

Database hosts that connect out to DumpCat over HTTPS instead of opening a port.

#### `GET /api/agents`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

List the agents and whether they are connected.

#### `POST /api/agents`

admin · full-access token

Create an agent. Answers its key and install commands once.

#### `PUT /api/agents/{id}`

admin · full-access token

Update an agent (name, allowed addresses, physical backups).

#### `POST /api/agents/{id}/rotate`

admin · full-access token

Give the agent a new key; the old one stops working.

#### `DELETE /api/agents/{id}`

admin · full-access token

Delete an agent.

### WireGuard

The built-in WireGuard server that database hosts can join.

#### `GET /api/wireguard`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

WireGuard state, settings and peers.

#### `PUT /api/wireguard`

admin · full-access token

Turn WireGuard on or off and change its settings.

#### `POST /api/wireguard/peers`

admin · full-access token

Add a peer. Answers its configuration file once.

#### `PUT /api/wireguard/peers/{id}`

admin · full-access token

Update a peer.

#### `POST /api/wireguard/peers/{id}/rotate`

admin · full-access token

Give the peer new keys. Answers its new configuration once.

#### `DELETE /api/wireguard/peers/{id}`

admin · full-access token

Delete a peer.

### Storage

Where backups go. Secret fields come back as `__SECRET_UNCHANGED__`: send that value back to keep the stored secret.

#### `GET /api/storage-types`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

The storage types and their fields, and the OAuth callback URL.

#### `GET /api/storages`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

List the storages.

#### `POST /api/storages`

operator · full-access token

Add a storage (`name`, `type`, `config`).

#### `POST /api/storages/test`

operator · full-access token

Test unsaved settings: write, read and delete a file.

#### `GET /api/storages/{id}`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

One storage.

#### `PUT /api/storages/{id}`

operator · full-access token

Update a storage.

#### `DELETE /api/storages/{id}`

operator · full-access token

Delete a storage.

#### `POST /api/storages/{id}/test`

operator · full-access token

Test a saved storage: write, read and delete a file.

#### `GET /api/storages/{id}/browse`

operator · read-only or full-access token

List the folders and files under `path`.

#### `GET /api/storages/{id}/usage`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

The space DumpCat's backups take there.

#### `POST /api/storages/{id}/import`

operator · full-access token

Import the backup catalog: list again the backups found on the storage (after a reinstall).

#### `POST /api/oauth/start`

operator · full-access token

Start the OAuth sign-in of a Google Drive, OneDrive or Dropbox storage.

#### `POST /api/oauth/exchange`

operator · full-access token

Finish an OAuth sign-in with a pasted code.

#### `GET /api/oauth/result`

operator · full-access token

The result of an OAuth sign-in (`state`).

#### `GET /api/oauth/callback`

viewer · full-access token

Where the provider sends the browser back after an OAuth sign-in.

### Notifications

Channels (email, Telegram, Slack, Discord, webhooks) that report failures, successes and alerts.

#### `GET /api/notify-types`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

The channel types and their fields.

#### `GET /api/notifications`

admin · read-only or full-access token

List the channels.

#### `POST /api/notifications`

admin · full-access token

Add a channel.

#### `PUT /api/notifications/{id}`

admin · full-access token

Update a channel.

#### `DELETE /api/notifications/{id}`

admin · full-access token

Delete a channel.

#### `POST /api/notifications/{id}/test`

admin · full-access token

Send a test message through a saved channel.

#### `POST /api/notifications/test`

admin · full-access token

Send a test message with unsaved settings.

#### `POST /api/notifications/digest`

admin · full-access token

Send the weekly digest now through a channel.

#### `GET /api/digest/preview`

admin · read-only or full-access token

The weekly digest as it would be sent now.

### Users

#### `GET /api/users`

admin · read-only or full-access token

List the accounts.

#### `POST /api/users`

admin · full-access token

Create an account. Body: `{"username", "email", "password", "role"}` (viewer, operator or admin).

#### `PUT /api/users/{id}`

admin · full-access token

Change an account: any of `email`, `role`, `disabled`, `password`. Locking it or setting a password ends its sessions and revokes its tokens.

#### `DELETE /api/users/{id}`

admin · full-access token

Delete an account.

#### `POST /api/users/{id}/reset-2fa`

admin · full-access token

Turn two-factor sign-in off for an account that lost its authenticator.

### Your account and API tokens

#### `GET /api/me`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

The account the request is made as: id, username, email, role, two-factor state.

#### `POST /api/me/password`

viewer · full-access token

Change your password. Body: `{"current", "new"}`. Signs out your other sessions.

#### `POST /api/me/totp/setup`

viewer · full-access token

Start two-factor setup: answers the secret, the otpauth URL and a QR code.

#### `POST /api/me/totp/enable`

viewer · full-access token

Finish two-factor setup. Body: `{"code": "123456"}`.

#### `POST /api/me/totp/disable`

viewer · full-access token

Turn two-factor sign-in off. Body: `{"password"}`.

#### `GET /api/me/tokens`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

Your API tokens: name, prefix, access, created, last used, expiry. Never the token itself.

#### `POST /api/me/tokens`

viewer · full-access token

Create a token. Body: `{"name", "access": "read", "full" or "manage", "expires_days" (0 = never), "password"}`. Answers `{"token": "mv_…", "item": {…}}`: the token is shown only in this answer.

#### `DELETE /api/me/tokens/{id}`

viewer · full-access token

Revoke one of your tokens.

#### `POST /api/me/logout-others`

viewer · full-access token

Sign out your other browser sessions.

### Settings and system

#### `GET /api/settings`

admin · read-only or full-access token

The settings (secrets masked).

#### `PUT /api/settings`

admin · full-access token

Change the settings (send the whole object).

#### `POST /api/settings/metrics-token`

admin · full-access token

Create or replace the bearer token of `GET /metrics`. Answers it once.

#### `GET /api/branding/logo`

public · no token needed

The instance's logo with its own Content-Type (PNG, WebP or SVG); redirects to the cat when none is set. The instance name is the `instance_name` setting.

#### `PUT /api/branding/logo`

admin · full-access token

Upload a logo. Body: `{"data": "<base64 or a data: URL>"}`; PNG, WebP or a plain SVG drawing (no scripts, links or external files), at most 256 KB. Answers the name and the logo URL.

#### `DELETE /api/branding/logo`

admin · full-access token

Go back to the default logo.

#### `GET /api/settings/sso`

admin · read-only or full-access token

The single sign-on (OpenID Connect) settings, the client secret masked, and `redirect_url`: the callback to register at the provider.

#### `PUT /api/settings/sso`

admin · full-access token

Change the SSO settings: `{"enabled", "issuer", "client_id", "client_secret", "scopes", "allowed_domains", "auto_create", "default_role", "role_claim", "admin_values", "operator_values", "viewer_values", "password_admins_only", ...}`. Turning it on checks that the provider answers.

#### `POST /api/settings/sso/test`

admin · full-access token

Start a test sign-in with the SSO settings in the body (saved or not). Answers `{"url"}` to open in a browser: the page it ends on shows the verified claims and what a sign-in would do, and signs nobody in.

#### `GET /api/system`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

Version, platform, uptime, data directory and the backup tools found with their versions.

#### `POST /api/system/tools/refresh`

admin · full-access token

Look for the backup tools again.

#### `GET /api/update`

admin · read-only or full-access token

The installed and the latest version, and the state of an update.

#### `POST /api/update/check`

admin · full-access token

Check for a new version now.

#### `POST /api/update/install`

admin · full-access token

Install the latest version (waits for running backups, rolls back on failure).

#### `POST /api/update/cancel`

admin · full-access token

Cancel an update that has not started installing.

#### `POST /api/update/rollback`

admin · full-access token

Go back to the version before the last update.

#### `GET /api/audit`

admin · read-only or full-access token

The audit log, newest first. Query: `q` (search), `limit` (default 100), `offset`.

### AI assistants and this reference

#### `POST /api/mcp`

public · any API token

The MCP endpoint (streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC, no sessions). API tokens only, see *AI assistants (MCP)* above.

#### `GET /api/mcp/tools`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

The MCP tools with what each does and the role and token access it needs.

#### `GET /api/docs.md`

viewer · read-only or full-access token

This reference, in Markdown.

### Signing in (web UI)

The browser's sign-in. Scripts and assistants use an API token instead.

#### `GET /api/auth/status`

public · no token needed

Whether setup is needed and whether this browser is signed in.

#### `POST /api/auth/setup`

public · no token needed

Create the first admin with the one-time setup token, while no account exists.

#### `POST /api/auth/login`

public · no token needed

Sign in and get a session cookie. Body: `{"username", "password", "totp", "remember"}`; answers `{"totp_required": true}` when a two-factor code is needed.

#### `POST /api/auth/logout`

public · no token needed

End the browser session.

#### `GET /api/auth/sso/start`

public · no token needed

Sign in with single sign-on: redirects the browser to the identity provider (`?remember=1` keeps the session 30 days).

#### `GET /api/auth/sso/callback`

public · no token needed

Where the identity provider sends the browser back: checks the state, the code (PKCE) and the ID token, then signs in.

#### `POST /api/auth/sso/totp`

public · no token needed

Finish an SSO sign-in with the two-factor code of an account that has 2FA. Body: `{"totp"}`.

### Outside /api

#### `GET /metrics`

Prometheus metrics, off until enabled in **Settings → Monitoring** (its own bearer token, or this machine only).

methods.title: mysqldump / mariadb-dump
methods.description: Single-threaded logical backup with --single-transaction (no InnoDB locking). Most flexible: restore individual databases, rename them, move across versions. Best for databases under ~50 GB.
methods.threads: mysqldump: number of databases dumped in parallel
methods.users_help: Saved as a separate _users.sql file; restoring it is optional.

methods.title: mydumper / myloader
methods.description: Multi-threaded logical backup that splits large tables into chunks; parallel restore is many times faster. Best for large databases that still need logical restores.
methods.users_help: Saved as a separate _users.sql file; restoring it is optional.

methods.title: Physical (XtraBackup / MariaBackup)
methods.description: Copies data files while the database is running (hot backup, no InnoDB locking), with incremental support. Fastest for very large databases (100 GB–TB); restore is a file copy. Runs on the database server: DumpCat installed there, or an agent started with --allow-physical.
methods.threads: Number of files copied in parallel (--parallel)

restore_options.label: Drop target databases before restoring
restore_options.help: DROP DATABASE, then recreate. Unchecked: tables in the dump are recreated (DROP TABLE IF EXISTS) but other tables are left untouched.

restore_options.label: Fast mode
restore_options.help: Temporarily sets innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit=2 & sync_binlog=0 during the restore, then restores them — much faster for large databases.

restore_options.label: Don't write binlog (sql_log_bin=0)
restore_options.help: The restore (including DROP/CREATE DATABASE) is not replicated to replicas. Requires SUPER / SYSTEM_VARIABLES_ADMIN — without it the restore stops before changing anything.

restore_options.label: Restore users & grants
restore_options.help: Runs _users.sql (CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS + GRANT).

restore_options.label: Remove DEFINER from views, routines, triggers and events
restore_options.help: They are created with the restore account as definer. Needed when the original accounts don't exist on the target, or the restore user lacks SET_USER_ID / SUPER.

restore_options.label: Convert collations the target may not know
restore_options.help: MySQL 8 `utf8mb4_0900_*` and MariaDB `*_uca1400_*` → `utf8mb4_unicode_ci` / `utf8mb4_bin`; `utf8mb3_*` → `utf8_*`. Needed for MySQL 8 → MariaDB or MySQL 5.7.

restore_options.label: Skip GTID_PURGED
restore_options.help: Drops `SET @@GLOBAL.GTID_PURGED` from the dump: it fails on a server with its own GTID history and needs SUPER. Keep it only to build a replica of the source.

methods.title: pg_dump (directory format)
methods.description: Logical backup of each database with pg_dump --format=directory, tables dumped in parallel from one consistent snapshot. Restore individual databases, rename them, restore onto newer PostgreSQL versions with pg_restore (also in parallel).
methods.threads: pg_dump / pg_restore --jobs: tables dumped and restored in parallel (one database at a time)
methods.users_help: Saved as a separate _globals.sql file; restoring it creates the roles the target does not have. Passwords need a superuser backup account.

methods.title: pg_basebackup (physical)
methods.description: Copies the whole cluster while it runs (every database, role and setting) over a replication connection: nothing to install on the database host. The base of WAL archiving and point-in-time recovery. A restore prepares a data directory on the DumpCat host and can replace a local cluster.
methods.threads: Not used: pg_basebackup copies the cluster in one stream

restore_options.label: Drop target databases before restoring
restore_options.help: DROP DATABASE, then create it again. Unchecked: a database that exists keeps its other objects; the objects in the backup are dropped and recreated (`pg_restore --clean --if-exists`). Sessions connected to a database stop the drop.

restore_options.label: Restore roles
restore_options.help: Creates the roles of _globals.sql that the target does not have yet, with their attributes and memberships. Existing roles, the restore account and `pg_*` roles are left alone; tablespaces are not created.

restore_options.label: Skip ownership (--no-owner)
restore_options.help: Objects belong to the restore account instead of their original owners. Needed when those roles don't exist on the target.

restore_options.label: Skip privileges (--no-privileges)
restore_options.help: No GRANT/REVOKE from the backup. Needed when the roles they name don't exist on the target.

methods.title: Native backup (BACKUP DATABASE)
methods.description: SQL Server's own full and differential backups of each database, WITH CHECKSUM and compressed where the edition allows, checked with RESTORE VERIFYONLY. SQL Server writes them into its backup folder, DumpCat moves them to the job's storages. Restore databases under new names or onto other servers; scheduled log backups add point-in-time recovery.
methods.threads: Databases backed up at the same time (each one needs room in the backup folder until DumpCat has read it)

restore_options.label: Replace existing databases (WITH REPLACE)
restore_options.help: A database of the same name is overwritten: its sessions are closed (`SET SINGLE_USER WITH ROLLBACK IMMEDIATE`), then `RESTORE … WITH REPLACE` reuses its files. Unchecked, a restore onto a name that exists stops before anything is changed.

mcp_tools.name: get_overview
mcp_tools.title: DumpCat overview
mcp_tools.description: Start here. A summary of this DumpCat: version; how many servers, jobs and backups; every job's last result, last successful backup, freshness and next run; the tasks running now (backups, verifications, restores, drills) with progress; the 12 most recent backups; and the current warnings (failed jobs, overdue backups, log archiving problems, failed restore drills).

mcp_tools.name: get_monitoring
mcp_tools.title: Monitoring status and alerts
mcp_tools.description: Monitoring status and alerts: for every job, whether its newest successful backup is fresh or overdue (stale, due_at: the same rule as DumpCat's freshness alerts and /metrics); the state of continuous log archiving (MySQL binlogs, PostgreSQL WAL, SQL Server log backups): streaming or failing, files waiting for upload, archive lag; and the active warnings. Use it to answer "is everything backed up?".

mcp_tools.name: list_servers
mcp_tools.title: List database servers
mcp_tools.description: The database servers DumpCat backs up or restores to: engine (mysql = MySQL, MariaDB, Percona; postgres = PostgreSQL; mssql = SQL Server), address, user, TLS mode, detected version, and how DumpCat reaches them (directly, or through an agent or WireGuard peer by id). Passwords are never returned (has_password tells whether one is saved).

mcp_tools.name: get_server
mcp_tools.title: Get a database server
mcp_tools.description: One database server. With check_connection, DumpCat also connects to it now (a few seconds) and reports whether it can, the version, databases with sizes, privileges, warnings, and which backup methods work from here — the first thing to check when backups of a server fail to connect.

mcp_tools.name: list_jobs
mcp_tools.title: List backup jobs
mcp_tools.description: The backup jobs: server, method, databases, schedules (cron), compression, encryption, storage targets, retention, options (verification, log archiving, max age), enabled or running, the last run, the next run and the last restore drill.

mcp_tools.name: get_job
mcp_tools.title: Get a backup job
mcp_tools.description: One backup job with its configuration, whether it is running, its last run, next run and last restore drill.

mcp_tools.name: list_backups
mcp_tools.title: List backups
mcp_tools.description: Backups (each run of a job), newest first, with total for paging. status success or partial: a backup that can be restored or verified; failed and canceled: error says why; queued and running: in progress. The id is what get_backup, get_log, verify_backup and plan_pitr take.

mcp_tools.name: get_backup
mcp_tools.title: Get a backup
mcp_tools.description: One backup in detail: status, error, timings, sizes, its databases and files, where it is stored and the state of each copy, its verification and restore drill results, its incremental chain, and live progress while it runs.

mcp_tools.name: get_log
mcp_tools.title: Read the end of a log
mcp_tools.description: The last lines of a task's log, to see why something failed or how far it got. kind backup takes a backup id, restore a restore id, drill_run a drill run id, log_archive a job id (its binlog/WAL archiver).

mcp_tools.name: list_restores
mcp_tools.title: List restores
mcp_tools.description: Restores that were run from the web UI or API, newest first: backup, target server, status and error. Restore drills are listed by list_drill_runs.

mcp_tools.name: get_restore
mcp_tools.title: Get a restore
mcp_tools.description: One restore: backup, target server, options, status, error, and live progress while it runs.

mcp_tools.name: list_drills
mcp_tools.title: List restore drills
mcp_tools.description: Restore drills: tests that restore a job's backup into a sandbox server under temporary names and check it (tables, row counts, SQL assertions, time to restore). Each with its schedule, last result, next run, and configuration problems.

mcp_tools.name: list_drill_runs
mcp_tools.title: List restore drill runs
mcp_tools.description: Results of restore drills, newest first: passed, failed or partial (temporary databases left behind), with summary and error.

mcp_tools.name: get_drill_run
mcp_tools.title: Get a restore drill run
mcp_tools.description: One restore drill run: every check with its result, restore and check durations, the databases, temporary databases left behind, the error, and live progress while it runs.

mcp_tools.name: plan_pitr
mcp_tools.title: Preview a point-in-time recovery
mcp_tools.description: Preview a point-in-time recovery; nothing is changed or restored. DumpCat picks the base backup for the target and checks that the archived log (MySQL binlogs, PostgreSQL WAL, SQL Server log backups) reaches it, with warnings. Give job_id (or backup_id for a given base). target_type latest or time (RFC 3339, e.g. 2026-10-20T09:30:00+07:00) work for every engine; position (file and pos) and gtid for MySQL; lsn and name (a restore point) for PostgreSQL; lsn and mark (name: a marked transaction) for SQL Server. The recovery itself is started in the web UI. Needs the operator role.

mcp_tools.name: run_backup
mcp_tools.title: Run a backup now
mcp_tools.description: Start a backup of a job now, like Run now in the web UI, and return the new backup (its id is for get_backup and get_log; it runs in the background). type incremental is taken only by methods that have incremental backups, differential by SQL Server's native backups (incremental means differential there), otherwise a full backup runs. Afterwards the job's retention may remove old backups, as after a scheduled run. Needs the operator role and a token with full access.

mcp_tools.name: verify_backup
mcp_tools.title: Verify a backup
mcp_tools.description: Check a stored backup: read every copy (or one location) back from storage and compare each file's checksum. Runs in the background; get_backup shows verify_status and verify_msg when it ends. Only successful or partial backups. Needs the operator role and a token with full access.

mcp_tools.name: start_drill
mcp_tools.title: Start a restore drill
mcp_tools.description: Run a restore drill now: restore a backup (the newest usable one, or backup_id) into the drill's sandbox server under temporary names, run its checks, then drop the temporary databases. Nothing on the source server is touched. Returns the drill run; follow it with get_drill_run and get_log. Needs the operator role and a token with full access.

mcp_tools.name: list_storages
mcp_tools.title: List storages
mcp_tools.description: Where backups are stored: local folders, S3, Google Drive, OneDrive, SFTP and the others, with the result of their last test and the jobs that use them. The id is what jobs' targets take.

mcp_tools.name: get_storage
mcp_tools.title: Get a storage
mcp_tools.description: One storage with its settings (secrets never: secrets_set and secrets_not_set name them) and the result of its last test.

mcp_tools.name: list_storage_types
mcp_tools.title: List storage types
mcp_tools.description: The kinds of storage DumpCat writes to and the settings of each (for create_storage): key, label, whether required, default, choices, and show_if (the setting applies only when another has one of these values). Settings marked secret are entered by the user in the web UI, never over MCP. local and rclone storages need the admin role.

mcp_tools.name: preview_schedule
mcp_tools.title: Preview a schedule
mcp_tools.description: Check a cron expression for a job or drill schedule and show its next five times in DumpCat's time zone; changes nothing.

mcp_tools.name: test_storage
mcp_tools.title: Test a storage
mcp_tools.description: Check a storage's settings and credentials now: write, read back and delete a small test file. Returns ok, or the error. Needs the operator role and a token with full access.

mcp_tools.name: create_server
mcp_tools.title: Add a database server
mcp_tools.description: Add a database server to back up (or to restore drills into). No password is taken: when the account needs one, the user enters it at finish_url in the web UI; then get_server with check_connection shows the version, databases, missing privileges and which backup methods work. Needs the operator role and a token with Manage access.

mcp_tools.name: update_server
mcp_tools.title: Change a database server
mcp_tools.description: Change a database server's settings; only the ones given change. Moving a server with a saved password to another host, port, socket or user, or weakening its TLS, needs the password again: that change is made in the web UI. Needs the operator role and a token with Manage access.

mcp_tools.name: create_storage
mcp_tools.title: Add a storage
mcp_tools.description: Add a storage that backups are written to, with its settings from list_storage_types. Secrets (access keys, passwords, OAuth tokens) are never taken: the answer lists the ones not set and finish_url, where the user enters them. Then test_storage. local and rclone storages need the admin role. Needs the operator role and a token with Manage access.

mcp_tools.name: update_storage
mcp_tools.title: Change a storage
mcp_tools.description: Rename a storage or change its settings; only the ones given change and saved secrets stay. Pointing a storage with saved secrets at another host, endpoint, account or user needs the secrets again: that change is made in the web UI. Needs the operator role and a token with Manage access.

mcp_tools.name: create_job
mcp_tools.title: Create a backup job
mcp_tools.description: Create a backup job: which server, method, databases, when (cron), where to (storages) and how many to keep. Settings not given are those of the web UI's new-job form (daily at 02:00, zstd, keep 7, verify one copy, notify on failure). The job backs up on its schedule from now on unless enabled is false; run_backup starts one now. Pre/post commands, extra tool arguments and the encryption passphrase are set in the web UI (finish_url). Needs the operator role and a token with Manage access.

mcp_tools.name: update_job
mcp_tools.title: Change a backup job
mcp_tools.description: Change a backup job; only the settings given change (options and retention key by key; targets is the whole list). enabled false pauses it. Lowering retention removes older backups after the next backup. Encryption, the passphrase, pre/post commands and extra tool arguments are changed in the web UI. Needs the operator role and a token with Manage access.

mcp_tools.name: create_drill
mcp_tools.title: Create a restore drill
mcp_tools.description: Create a restore drill: on a schedule, restore a job's newest backup into a sandbox server under temporary names, check tables, row counts and SQL assertions, then drop the copies. Settings not given are those of the web UI's form (Sundays at 05:00, notify on failure). start_drill runs it now. Needs the operator role and a token with Manage access.

mcp_tools.name: update_drill
mcp_tools.title: Change a restore drill
mcp_tools.description: Change a restore drill; only the settings given change (options key by key; assertions is the whole list). enabled false pauses it. Needs the operator role and a token with Manage access.
